parameters.content:
# 02 - HubSpot Sync

## What this workflow does

The **only** place the automated pipeline writes to the CRM. (Workflow 06 also writes, but only when a rep clicks a button - never automatically.) Workflow 01 calls it once the lead has been classified and synthesised, and only when the scan carried a valid email: without one there is no safe dedupe key, so the write is skipped rather than guessed.

**02A is the read half of this pair.** It runs earlier in the same pipeline to gather CRM context *before* enrichment and AI; 02 performs every write *after*. Separating them is what stops a lookup from mutating a record, and what lets the model see the CRM without being able to touch it.

This workflow makes the contact, the company and the booth history correct and deduplicated, then hands the resolved `crm_context` back so the Slack card can link to the real record and show the real owner.

## Hypotheses this design rests on

1. **Email is the contact identity.** Scanning the same badge twice must never create a second contact. This is the task's explicit dedupe requirement, and it is enforced by upserting on email rather than creating.
2. **Domain is the company identity.** One company per domain, which is what makes "two people from one company" cheap in enrichment too.
3. **A human in HubSpot beats a scanner.** Anything a person already typed is preserved; the automation only fills blanks. A booth scanner should never overwrite a rep's own work.
4. **An orphaned contact is not a clean CRM.** Post-event playbooks segment by company, so a company record is created when the domain is new.
5. **The CRM beats enrichment.** A headcount found on the web is written only when HubSpot has none.

## The logic that is implemented

**Order matters, and it is company-first:** find company by exact domain → create it or enrich it → find contact by email → read genuinely associated deals → resolve owner names → upsert the contact and associate it → patch the Oak properties → log a meeting and a readable note.

**What is written, precisely:**

| Target | Fields | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Contact | `firstname`, `lastname`, `jobtitle`, `company`, `website`, `lifecyclestage`, `hs_lead_status` | only when HubSpot is blank |
| Contact | 18 `oak_*` properties incl. `oak_lead_tier`, `oak_persona`, `oak_lead_score`, `oak_decision_reasons` | always |
| Company | `name`, `domain` | on create |
| Company | `numberofemployees` | only when the CRM has none |
| Engagements | one meeting + one associated note | every scan |

**Deals use the documented v4 associations endpoint**, then a v3 batch read - so "open deals" means deals genuinely associated to this company, not a text search that happens to match.

**Industry is deliberately not written to the company.** HubSpot's `industry` is a fixed enumeration (`BANKING`, `COMPUTER_SOFTWARE`, …). Mapping a resolved value onto it would be a guess that silently corrupts segmentation, so resolved industry lives on the contact as `oak_industry` with `oak_industry_source`, and in the note with its URL.

**No follow-up task is created here.** The Slack *Snooze* action is the only task creator in the whole system, so nothing invents an SLA nobody agreed to.

## Where it can fail

Every HubSpot call soft-fails and reports. A failed company create becomes a visible warning rather than a silent orphaned contact; a failed property patch is reported in `crm_context.warnings` and surfaces on the Slack card. The contact write is the one step whose failure means the lead is not in the CRM, and that is stated explicitly in the delivery receipt.

**The Oak property patch is all-or-nothing.** All 18 go out in one PATCH, so one value HubSpot refuses loses all 18. That is not hypothetical: `oak_competitor_status` is an enumeration accepting only `none` / `possible` / `confirmed`, and while this node sent a decorated `confirmed: Veza` HubSpot answered `400 INVALID_OPTION` and discarded the tier, persona, score and reasons along with it. A competitor's actual name belongs in the booth note, not in an enum. For the same reason `oak_rule_summary` and `oak_score_breakdown` are computed but never sent - they are not provisioned in the portal, so their content is prepended to `oak_decision_reasons`, which is written. That whole class of failure is only visible because `crm_context.oak_properties_written` is asserted from the response body rather than assumed from the node having run.

## What a rep has already done survives the next scan

This is hypothesis 3 as code rather than as intent. Five free-text contact fields go through a single `keep()` helper - the existing HubSpot value wins and the scan only fills a blank - and `lifecyclestage` and `hs_lead_status` reach the same result their own way, defaulting only for a contact that does not exist yet.

The rep's own event fields are carried forward rather than reset: `oak_booth_status`, `oak_claimed_by` and `oak_claimed_at` are read off the existing contact and written straight back, so a lead somebody claimed and marked *met* does not quietly return to `scanned` on the next badge scan. `oak_exclude_from_outreach` is sticky in one direction only - a competitor match can set it and a rep can set it, but no scan ever clears it.

nodes.name: Resolve Company Write
nodes.notes: Decides whether the company must be created, updated with enriched headcount, or left alone. HubSpot's industry field is a fixed enumeration, so resolved industry is deliberately not written here; it lives on the contact as oak_industry and in the booth note.

nodes.name: Create or Update Company
nodes.notes: One node handles create, enrich-update and no-op by taking its method, URL and body from the planner above. A no-identity scan targets company 0 and 404s harmlessly.

nodes.name: Resolve Company Id
nodes.notes: Settles the company id the contact will be associated to, and turns a failed company write into a visible warning rather than a silent orphan.

nodes.name: Get Company Deal Associations
nodes.notes: Documented v4 associations endpoint. Replaces the associations.company search filter, which n8n flagged because it is a search key rather than a real deal property.

nodes.name: Read Associated Deals

nodes.notes: Batch-reads only the deals actually associated to this company. A company with no deals sends no ids and soft-fails to an empty result.

nodes.name: List HubSpot Owners
nodes.notes: One cheap call per sync. Free portals have a handful of owners, so fetching the list beats a lookup per id and gives the card a name instead of a number.
